I've been growing cotton on these 10 mu for 10 years now. I went to middle school and then came back to the village to farm. Last year my yield was about 500 kg per mu, which was decent but not great. My neighbor Lao Zhang used Guoxinmian improved seed and got 600 kg per mu, so this year I will switch to that same seed. I need 2.5 jin of seed per mu — 25 jin total for my 10.1 mu.

For fertilizer, I hire a rotary tiller in late March, costs me 50 yuan per mu. I put down 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer as base, the special high-potassium type, 20-10-21. Cotton needs potassium for the bolls, more than wheat or corn. That's 20 bags at about 100 yuan each. When the plants flower in July, I topdress with another 50 jin per mu of urea, 5 bags. All together that works out to about 20 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 18 kg of potassium per mu.

I have a well, so I irrigate three times: once right after sowing in late April to get the seedlings standing, once at flowering in July, and once in August when the bolls are filling. Diesel for the pump costs about 30 yuan each time.

Pesticide is the biggest headache on cotton. I spray 12 times. First for aphids when the seedlings have three leaves, then for bollworm every two weeks through summer, and for red spider mite in August when it turns dry. Each spray costs about 15 yuan per mu. Better to spray too much than lose the crop — one bad bollworm year and you lose everything. I also do one herbicide spray before planting.

My household has four people. My wife works in the field with me, and my younger brother works in a factory in Shijiazhuang. His off-farm wages help pay for the fertilizer and pesticide. I expect 550 kg per mu this year.
